title: dareskro
subtitle: Pay that pays itself. On the XRP Ledger.
narration: Dareskro. Pay that pays itself, on the XRP Ledger. Four examples, one rule.

title: One rule
subtitle: A human decides. Code calculates. The ledger pays.
narration: The rule is simple. A human decides. Code calculates. The ledger pays. And an oracle opens the door at the right moment, with no power over the money.

title: 1 · The pharmacist
subtitle: Sunday shift, 9 to 21. Badge: 12 h 12. Retained: 12 h.
narration: Example one. A pharmacist works a Sunday shift. The badge proves he was there: twelve hours and twelve minutes. The schedule qualifies the hours: twelve. An agent reads both. The badge never qualifies an hour; only the schedule does.

title: Code computes
narration: Code computes the pay from the collective agreement, line by line. Shift time, overtime, Sunday allowance, seniority bonus. Four hundred sixty-six euros fifty-seven. Replayable to the cent, three years later.

title: A human signs on a Ledger device
subtitle: Amount · Destination · Pay date · Hash · Oracle
narration: A named person validates the statement. Then the employer signs the escrow on a Ledger device. The device shows the amount, the destination, the pay date, the hash of the statement, and the name of the oracle. Nothing moves before that signature.

title: The oracle, in real life
subtitle: An account. A birth certificate. A small program.
narration: So what is the oracle, in real life? Three things. An account on the XRP Ledger, with a name. A birth certificate: one transaction that says what it is, for anyone to read. And a small program that watches the escrows it is cited in.

title: One job
subtitle: Wait for the date. Submit the finish. Pay 12 drops.
narration: Its only job: wait for the pay date, submit the finish, pay the fee. Twelve drops. It never holds the money. The ledger moves the four hundred sixty-six euros from the employer's escrow to the employee.

title: What it cannot do
subtitle: Pay early: refused. Redirect: no field. Cancel: nothing to cancel.
narration: What it cannot do, by construction, not by promise. Pay early: the ledger refuses. Redirect: there is no such field. Cancel: the escrow has no cancel date. We tried all three on testnet. All three failed.

title: If the oracle dies
subtitle: Anyone can finish after the date. The employee too.
narration: And if the oracle dies? Anyone can finish the escrow after the date. The employee himself. The money goes where it was written. A good oracle is useful, and not needed.

title: 2 · The real-estate agent
subtitle: Nothing at the preliminary contract. Everything at the deed. Oracle: the notary.
narration: Example two. A real-estate agent. Nothing is owed at the preliminary contract, everything at the deed. The escrow holds the commission behind a secret. The oracle is the notary: party to nothing. And the sale is published afterwards, so anyone can check.

title: 3 · The freelancer
subtitle: Lagos and Paris. Released on proof of delivery. Oracle: the service.
narration: Example three. A freelancer in Lagos, a client in Paris. The oracle holds the secret and reveals it when delivery is proven. It cannot steal: the money goes to the written destination. It can only block, and blocking ends at the deadline, with a refund.

title: 4 · Affiliate commissions
subtitle: One escrow per sale. Oracle: the merchant's system, or none at all.
narration: Example four. Affiliate commissions. One escrow per expected sale, released by the merchant's sales system, automatically. The merchant is a party, so the money is locked before the sale. Or no oracle at all: the customer pays through dareskro and the commission splits at source.

title: The question that sorts oracles
subtitle: Is it a party to the dispute?
narration: The question that sorts oracles is not whether it can disappear. It is whether it is a party to the dispute. An oracle with a stake is not an oracle. We put it where it has nothing to gain, or we remove it.

title: The agent pays for its evidence
subtitle: 0.05 RLUSD a query · Mastercard Agent Pay for Machines · inside a cap
narration: One more thing. The agent buys the collective-agreement rules it needs. Five cents a query, on Mastercard Agent Pay for Machines, inside a budget the employer set. Nobody clicks. Every cent leaves a proof on the ledger.

title: Built this weekend, on testnet
subtitle: Signed on device. Released by the oracle alone. Paid by the agent alone.
narration: All of this ran this weekend on testnet. The escrow signed on the device. The oracle released it by itself, twelve seconds after the date. The agent paid by itself. Every step has a hash you can open.

title: dareskro
subtitle: The AI reads. Code calculates. A human signs. The ledger pays. Not before.
narration: Dareskro. The AI reads. Code calculates. A human signs. The ledger pays. Not before.
